about.title: King City Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Grief does not follow a schedule, but California law does. That tension is what makes wrongful death claims so hard for families in King City to face alone. A civil wrongful death action is separate from any criminal case the Monterey County District Attorney may bring; it exists so a family can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the harder-to-measure loss of love, companionship and guidance. Standing is limited: a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and far sooner when a government entity is involved. King City's 2025 public record shows 21 injury collisions and no traffic deaths, a reminder that these claims arise from many settings beyond the road, including workplaces, medical care and unsafe property. We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We can sort out who belongs in the claim before anyone misses a step.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general two-year deadline runs from the date of death, and claims against a city, county or state agency must be filed much sooner. We protect your family's options by moving quickly.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Our consultation is free, and we work on contingency. Your family should not have to weigh legal bills against grief.

items.question: King City recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Do wrongful death claims still happen here?
items.answer: Yes. Traffic collisions are only one source of these claims, and the 2025 public record for King City shows 21 injury collisions with 27 people injured and zero deaths. Wrongful death claims in a small Monterey County community also arise from farm and workplace accidents, medical negligence, unsafe property and defective equipment. The cause matters less than whether someone else's carelessness led to the loss.

items.question: What if a government agency may be responsible, such as a road condition on S 1st Street or a public vehicle?
items.answer: Claims against a city, county or state entity follow a separate, much shorter process than the standard two-year deadline. A formal claim usually has to be presented to the agency within months of the death, before any lawsuit can be filed. Because that window closes fast, your family should contact us as soon as you suspect public involvement.

items.question: How is a wrongful death case different from criminal charges against the person responsible?
items.answer: A criminal case is brought by the Monterey County District Attorney to punish conduct, and the family does not control it. A wrongful death claim is a civil action your family brings to recover funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. The two can proceed at the same time, and a civil claim can go forward even if no charges are filed.
